sources.rationale: req.params carries the decoded route parameters of the matched route — attacker-chosen URL path segments. The express.Request coordinate binds via type annotations; untyped handlers are covered by the stock native model.
req.query is the parsed query string — attacker-chosen keys and values, including nested objects under the extended parser.
req.body is the parsed request body (express.json / express.urlencoded) — wholly attacker-chosen.
req.cookies (cookie-parser middleware) exposes unsigned cookie values — client-chosen bytes.
req.headers (http.IncomingMessage) exposes raw request headers — client-chosen values behind common idioms like req.headers.referer.

sinks.rationale: res.redirect([status,] path) sets the Location header from its path argument — index 0 in the one-argument form, index 1 after a status code; an attacker URL is an open redirect.
res.location(path) sets the Location header directly; same open-redirect exposure as res.redirect without the implicit status.
res.sendFile(path) transfers the file at the given path; without the root option pinning a directory, attacker path segments serve files outside the intended tree.
res.download(path, ...) transfers the file at the given path as an attachment; same traversal exposure as res.sendFile.
res.send(body) with a string body responds text/html by default — reflected attacker text executes as markup.
